label: no
controls_available: Difficulty 1 uses a 5x5 board, 2 solution cells, at most 3 cells, 8 beats, and a 320 ms beat interval.
Full interaction drags the visible brass seed arrow onto an empty board cell (cell_drag) and clicks a placed arrow to cycle its direction clockwise (cell_click).
The UI also exposes RUN 8 BEATS, STEP ONE BEAT, CLEAR CONFIGURATION, REVISE STARTING ARROWS after a film, and CHECK SEQUENCE after completion; CHECK SEQUENCE is administrative.
While the film is running, edit, run, step, reset, and revision actions are disabled or ignored, so no outcome-affecting edit remains effective during the autonomous film.
autonomous_processes: After RUN FILM, the first beat is applied synchronously and subsequent beats run autonomously every 320 ms until all 8 beats complete.

Each autonomous beat moves arrows one square, reverses an arrow at a wall, turns an arrow clockwise for an occupied or duplicate destination, appends wall events, and visibly updates the board and event ledger.
At difficulty 1, wall-flash CSS is removed after up to 272 ms; this changes presentation only and not the graded board or event state.
STEP ONE BEAT advances the simulation synchronously on the button action; waiting between step actions does not advance the simulation.
grouped_control_modes: Full configuration editing: cell_drag placement and cell_click direction cycling in edit phase.
Autonomous-film start: RUN FILM starts the timed 8-beat simulation and leaves no effective outcome-affecting control during running.
Manual stepping: STEP ONE BEAT, where each beat changes synchronously only when the agent acts.
Post-film configuration control: REVISE STARTING ARROWS and CLEAR CONFIGURATION, available outside the running phase.
Administrative certification: CHECK SEQUENCE after the film completes.

clause_i.reason: For the full edit controls, target-specific cell locations and directions vary across generated instances while the prior action history I_t does not reveal the visible target ledger; an observation-free fixed edit policy cannot be optimal for every such history.

clause_ii.reason: A bounded current screenshot exposes the static target wall ledger and current board, so a policy can choose the next placement or direction cycle from visible state; the configured 600 ms observation window and 5 frames are more than sufficient for this static edit decision.

clause_iii.reason: The only nontrivial autonomous task-state evolution is the running film, but RUN FILM transitions out of edit phase and the browser gates or ignores cell_drag, cell_click, STEP, RESET, and REVISION during running. In edit phase there is no autonomous task-state change, and during manual stepping state changes only synchronously with the agent action. Wall-flash removal is presentation-only. Thus no legitimate grouped control mode has an available outcome-affecting action whose value strictly degrades during an autonomous interval.

common_visible_process: No common real-time witness exists. The running film visibly changes arrow positions, collision directions, wall flashes, and the accumulated ledger, but those frames only provide observation for a later revision; the configuration cannot be edited while that process runs and the resulting ledger remains available after completion.

pre_run.reason: The generator constructs target_events by simulating its generated solution_cells, and the browser permits all placement and direction edits before RUN FILM. The solver configures solution_cells first, runs the complete film, and submits only after completion; the grader independently re-simulates the configured cells and accepts the matching target. Therefore every generated instance admits a successful pre-run solution, without needing to claim a numeric rate.

source_evidence.claim: Difficulty 1 is the 5x5, two-solution-cell, eight-beat, 320 ms configuration with at most three cells.
The assigned full interaction is direct drag placement and placed-arrow clicking, with a 600 ms observation window and five frames.
The simulation advances one beat at a time, records wall impacts, reverses at walls, turns clockwise on encounters, and advances autonomously only as the film is run.
Each generated contract exposes the target wall events and stores solution_cells whose simulation defines that target.
Adding and rotating arrows both return unless phase is edit, and they record the full interaction edit transcript.
Grid drop and placed-arrow click handlers accept outcome-affecting full-input actions only in edit phase.
A beat updates simulated positions, collision turns, wall events, visible flashes, beat count, and event count.
RUN FILM applies the first beat immediately and schedules later beats with setTimeout at contract.beat_ms while phase is running.
Manual stepping applies a beat only on the button action, while reset and revision are unavailable during running.
The control state disables run/step/submit as appropriate and disables revision except after completion or manual stepping; running handlers reject edits.
The visible interface states that all edits happen before a film and that the film can be watched, compared, and revised afterward.
Wall flashes and failure/passed notices are CSS presentation effects; the wall-slot flash is not a separate graded control opportunity.
The full grader requires the full interaction sources, a completed eight-beat run, and a wall-event replay matching the target.
Grading independently simulates the configured cells and accepts only when the actual event sequence equals the target.
The solver's run-and-check path waits for the film to complete before submitting.
The successful path configures solution_cells before running the film and performs the submission only after completion.
The verifier loads the exported result and replays it through the independent collision-chimes grader.
